turns.prompt_text: what are some of the functionalities of Evernote the paid version
turns.response_html:
Evernote’s pricing structure has recently shifted away from the "Personal" and "Professional" labels you might be familiar with. In late 2025 and into 2026, they transitioned to two primary individual paid tiers: Starter and Advanced.

The most significant change in 2026 is that Evernote now imposes hard limits on the number of notes and notebooks even for paid users (on the Starter plan), whereas previously, paying usually meant "unlimited" everything.

Comparison of Paid Functionalities

FeatureStarter ($8.25 - $14.99/mo)Advanced (~$20 - $24/mo)
Note LimitUp to 1,000 notesUnlimited
NotebooksUp to 20 notebooksUnlimited
Device SyncUp to 3 devicesUnlimited
Storage1 GB monthly uploadUnlimited
AI FeaturesAI Edit, Cleanup, TranscribeFull AI Suite + AI Search
SearchInside PDFs, Office docs, imagesFull Semantic AI Search
IntegrationsGoogle Calendar (up to 5)Slack, MS Teams, Salesforce

Key Capabilities of the Paid Versions

1. AI-Powered Workflow

  • AI Transcribe: One of the more popular recent additions, this converts audio recordings or videos directly into text notes.
  • AI Edit & Cleanup: These tools help summarize long notes, fix formatting instantly, and "tidy up" messy brain-dumps into structured lists.
  • Semantic Search (Advanced Plan): Instead of just searching for keywords, you can ask questions like "What did I decide about the project last Tuesday?" and the AI finds the relevant context.

2. Advanced Search & OCR While the free version searches text, the paid versions index text inside PDFs, Office documents, and even photos of handwritten notes. This is a big deal for anyone using Evernote as a digital filing cabinet for receipts or whiteboard sessions.

3. Offline Access Paid tiers allow you to download entire notebooks to your phone or laptop. This is essential for traveling or working in areas with spotty service (like during a commute or on a flight).

4. Google Calendar Integration You can link your calendar to see your schedule directly inside Evernote. It allows you to create "Meeting Notes" with one click, which automatically pulls in the date, time, and attendee list from the event.

5. Customization & Power User Tools

  • Custom Templates: Create your own reusable structures for things like project specs or grocery lists.
  • PDF Annotation: Draw or type directly onto PDF attachments without leaving the app.
  • Boolean Search: Use complex search syntax (AND, OR, NOT) to find specific notes in a massive archive.

A Quick Reality Check

If you are currently on an old "Personal" or "Professional" plan, you will likely be migrated to the Advanced tier upon renewal. If you have more than 1,000 notes or 20 notebooks, you'll need the Advanced version to keep adding new content, as the Starter plan is now designed for more casual users.

turns.prompt_text: How does this compare to Notion or Obsidian, and why would I use it instead?
turns.response_html:
Choosing between Evernote, Notion, and Obsidian depends on whether you value a digital filing cabinet, a workspace for building systems, or a private "second brain."

1. Notion: The "All-in-One" Workspace

Notion is a modular database system. While Evernote is a collection of notes, Notion is a collection of pages that can contain databases, kanban boards, and linked wikis.

  • Structure: Everything is a "block." You can turn a simple list into a database with tags, dates, and formulas.
  • Strengths: Exceptional for collaboration and project management. It is much more powerful for building complex systems (like a habit tracker or a content calendar) than Evernote.
  • Weaknesses: The mobile app is often slower than Evernote’s, and because it is so flexible, it can be overwhelming to set up. It also requires an internet connection for most functions.

2. Obsidian: The Private "Second Brain"

Obsidian is a local-first application that stores notes as Markdown files on your hard drive. It is highly favored by developers and those who want total control over their data.

  • Structure: It uses "backlinks" and a "Graph View" to show how ideas connect across different notes, mimicking how the human brain associates information.
  • Strengths: It is incredibly fast, works completely offline, and has a massive library of community-made plugins. Your data is never locked into a proprietary format.
  • Weaknesses: It has a steeper learning curve. Syncing between a desktop and a phone usually requires a paid subscription (Obsidian Sync) or technical workarounds.

Why use Evernote instead?

Despite the rise of Notion and Obsidian, Evernote still holds a specific "pro-consumer" niche for a few reasons:

1. The "Web Clipper" Evernote’s browser extension is still considered the gold standard. It captures web pages, articles, and recipes perfectly, stripping out ads and preserving the layout. Notion’s clipper often struggles with complex formatting, and Obsidian requires third-party tools to do this effectively.

2. Superior Search & OCR Evernote is better at finding text inside images and PDFs. If you scan a physical receipt or take a photo of a whiteboard, Evernote’s OCR (Optical Character Recognition) makes that text searchable almost instantly. This makes it a better "digital filing cabinet" for paperless living.

3. Frictionless Capture Evernote is designed to get information in as fast as possible. The mobile app is optimized for quick voice memos, photos, and scratchpad notes. Notion often feels like you need to decide "where" a note goes before you write it, which can slow you down.

4. Email Integration With a paid Evernote plan, you get a unique email address. You can forward emails (like flight itineraries or receipts) directly to that address, and they appear as notes. Notion and Obsidian require more complex integrations to achieve this.

Summary Recommendation

  • Choose Evernote if you want a reliable, high-speed archive for documents, receipts, and web clips with powerful search.
  • Choose Notion if you need to manage projects, work with a team, or want to build a highly organized dashboard for your life.
  • Choose Obsidian if you are a "power user" who wants privacy, offline speed, and a way to link deep thoughts and research.

turns.prompt_text: So these three note-taking apps, and let's see Google Keep as well, all serve different functionality.
turns.response_html:
Spot on. They each focus on a different "style" of thinking and organizing. In the productivity world, these are often categorized by how they handle information: Librarian (Evernote), Architect (Notion), Gardener (Obsidian), and Sticky Notes (Google Keep).

Here is how Google Keep fits into that mix and why it’s often the "secret weapon" even for people who use the other three.

Google Keep: The "Sticky Note" Wall

If Evernote is a filing cabinet, Google Keep is the corkboard in your kitchen. It’s designed for speed and short-term memory.

  • Primary Use: Grocery lists, quick reminders ("Don't forget to buy solder flux"), and fleeting thoughts you’ll likely delete or move elsewhere within 48 hours.
  • The Killer Feature: Location-based reminders. You can set a note to ping your phone the moment you walk into a specific Fareway or Home Depot.
  • The Integration: Since you’re a heavy Google user, Keep’s integration with Gemini is its biggest 2026 upgrade. You can ask Gemini to "Summarize my 'Project Ideas' label in Keep" or "Add 'buy 18650 batteries' to my shopping list," and it happens instantly.

Why use one over the other? (The "Jobs to be Done" Framework)

Use CaseBest AppWhy?
"I need to remember this for 10 years."EvernoteIt’s built for archiving. The OCR makes sure you can find that one receipt from 2021 just by searching for a keyword on the paper.
"I need to build a system for my LLC."NotionYou can build a database of clients, link it to a project tracker, and view it as a Calendar or Kanban board. It’s a workspace, not just a notebook.
"I'm researching a complex topic."ObsidianAs someone who enjoys cross-disciplinary learning, Obsidian’s Graph View lets you see how a concept in computer science might link to a philosophy note you wrote months ago.
"I'm at the store and need my list."Google KeepZero friction. It opens instantly, works great with voice commands, and sits right in the sidebar of your Gmail and Google Calendar.

The "Pro" Workflow: Using Them Together

Many people—especially those in technical fields—don't choose just one. They use a pipeline:

  1. Capture (Keep): You’re out and have a random idea for a 3D print. You jot it in Keep.
  2. Process (Obsidian): Later, you sit at your desk and move that idea into Obsidian to research the mechanics and link it to your other projects.
  3. Execute (Notion): Once it becomes a real project for your software contracting work, you move the tasks into a Notion database to track deadlines and deliverables.
  4. Archive (Evernote): When the project is done, you throw the final PDF report and invoices into Evernote for long-term storage.

turns.prompt_text: How would that help me there?
turns.response_html:
Each of these apps offers a specific "edge" for the different hats you wear. Given you’re balancing a software contracting business, management shifts at Fareway, and complex DIY electronics, here is how those tools would specifically help you:

1. Managing Your Fareway Workflows

Since you've been developing an offline mobile workflow to handle your schedules and identify closing crews, Google Keep and Evernote are your strongest allies here.

  • Google Keep: Use this for "on-the-floor" friction. If you notice a stocking issue or a policy change while on a management shift, a quick voice note or photo in Keep is faster than opening a complex app.
  • Evernote: Use this as your "Policy Bible." Since you’re involved in management tasks, you can scan and OCR printed store memos or product code sheets. If you need to find a specific policy on "staffing levels" while standing in the aisle, Evernote’s search will find it inside a scanned PDF much faster than a standard file explorer.

2. Scaling Your Software Contracting

As you aim to land 2–3 independent contracts and manage legal documents like MSAs (Master Services Agreements), Notion is the clear winner for "Architecting" your business.

  • Client CRM: You can build a database to track your LinkedIn outreach, contract status (Sent, Signed, Paid), and project timelines.
  • Project Wiki: Instead of just having code in GitHub, you can use Notion to document "Customer Demands" and development processes for your website projects. It keeps the "business" side of the code organized in one dashboard.

3. DIY Electronics & "Polymath" Research

For your custom battery packs, 3D printing projects, and interest in cross-disciplinary learning, Obsidian is the best tool for the job.

  • The Second Brain: When you’re researching circuit analysis or beekeeping, you can "link" ideas. For example, a note on "Lithium-ion safety" can link to your project note for the "Milwaukee Battery Pack."
  • Offline/Dev Friendly: Since you’re comfortable in the terminal and using the fish shell, you’ll appreciate that Obsidian notes are just Markdown files. You can actually search, edit, or script your notes directly from your terminal if you want to.

4. Integration with Your Current Setup

Since you mentioned using the fish shell, you could actually use Obsidian or Google Keep in a very "dev-centric" way:

  • Obsidian CLI: You can write a quick fish function to open your daily project log in your favorite terminal editor (like Neovim) and have it instantly reflect in the Obsidian GUI.
  • Evernote for Reference: While you're at a hackathon (like the upcoming Amazon Nova one), you can use Evernote to quickly clip API documentation or technical articles so they are available offline and searchable when you're in the middle of a build.

Which "gap" feels most urgent right now?

  • Organization: Setting up a CRM in Notion to handle your new contracts?
  • Knowledge: Building a research library in Obsidian for your electronics and DIY projects?
  • Capture: Using Keep to stay on top of Fareway tasks?

I can help you set up a template or a folder structure for whichever one sounds most useful.
